body:
**Triage** — graded `p3`, `documentation`, `pm:queue`, routed `domain:skills`. (Applied and read back first.)

## Re-measured at `origin/main` `c616c2c` — confirmed, and one number is worse than filed

`skills/README.md`'s "Cross-skill routing" section carries exactly **4** decision points — lifecycle hooks vs. automation, screen flows vs. views, CEL expressions, kernel/plugin events vs. data lifecycle — and **none** is about labels vs. bundles. Verbatim as filed.

The sibling-skill measurement is stronger than you reported:

| skill | `translat` occurrences | you reported |
|---|---|---|
| `objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` | **0** | zero ✓ |
| `objectstack-data/SKILL.md` | **0** | "one passing mention" |

So both siblings are at zero. There is no passing mention to build on — an agent authoring a `label` in either package has *nothing* pointing at this domain, which is a slightly stronger case for the routing bullet than the card makes for itself.

## Why `p3` despite the usage numbers

Your usage measurement is the right evidence — 3 example apps, 40 `fields:` blocks, 37 `pluralLabel:` entries, 23 select-option label maps — and the failure mode you name is the real one: *"an untranslated label is a perfectly valid object"*, so no gate reports it and the agent never learns the domain applies.

It stays `p3` because nothing is broken and nothing is blocked; the cost is a capability that goes unused. A discoverability gap on a valid-but-suboptimal output is real debt, not urgency.

## Scope — and the budget is part of the ruling, not advice

**One bullet. ~25 tokens. In `skills/README.md` only.**

The maintainer's 2026-08-21 ruling applies and I am quoting it because it binds the size, not just the spirit: 「对外发布的 skills 是整个平台的最大价值,尤其要整体考虑和评估。」「……不能为了一个小功能扩写很多。」

⛔ Do not expand `objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` or `objectstack-data/SKILL.md` to mention translation. That is the tempting second edit and it is three files instead of one, in the two largest published skills, for a routing fact that belongs in the routing list. The zero-occurrence measurement above is a reason to add the bullet, ⛔ not a licence to fix the zeros.

⛔ Do not revisit the `objectstack-i18n` frontmatter description. #14315 already changed it, and your note on direction is exactly right: it helps the agent that has decided it is doing i18n work, while the bullet helps the agent that does not know the domain applies. Complements, not substitutes — so the bullet does not get re-argued as redundant.

## Merge path

`skills/**` is a governed surface: normal PR, **merged by hand by the maintainer**, ⛔ never approved by an agent seat, ⛔ never through the queue. Claimable now.

## On the filing

Giving this a tracked home rather than leaving it in a PR body was the right call, and the reason you give is the general one worth repeating: a follow-up recorded only in prose that merges and disappears is a follow-up nobody will do.
